pr.body:
closes #37118

PR is adding some context information to be available in the `access-token` without a need to introduce any additional custom claims. So far, it provides info about:

- session type (online, offline, transient), which was used to create the token
- token type (regular or lightweight token)
- grant type

These informations can be useful when token is later sent to some Keycloak endpoints (for example introspection, userInfo, admin/account REST API) to optimize something. For example:
- session-type will allow to lookup only correct session type based on the type of the session, which token was created from. As for example today, we need to lookup "online" session and if it is not found, then fallback to "offline" session. So possible unnecessary lookup. Related follow-up issue for optimize that: #37662

- Grant type knowledge can be useful for example for the token-exchange use-case: #37117

- Lightweight access token: We will be able to recognize more reliably if access-token is lightweight or not and do something based on that (EG. lookup roles from model instead of lookup roles from the token)

In this PR, I've made token ID to look something like `onrtac:1f65761e-1c69-40a2-82da-2d8aa5e39a8a` .
  - The first 2 characters is shortcut for "session type" - `on` is shortcut for "online" session
  - The next 2 characters is shortcut for "token type" - `rt` is shortcut for regular token (not lightweight token)
  - The next 2 characters is shortcut for grant type - `ac` is shortcut for "authorization code" grant

Shortcuts are used, so the token ID contains important info, but at the same time, it is limited in size and does not introduce much new characters to the token.

The encoding into ID is used only for access-tokens. Not used for refresh tokens or ID tokens or any others.

Introduced dedicated SPI in the end. Wanted to "cache" some objects (EG. shortcuts for grant types etc) and it seems clearer to me to cache them at the level of factory, rather than in the static fields, which is not very pretty. Moreover, provider adds ability for someone to introduce his own provider (and eventually encode some more info or encode stuff in the different way etc).

#### Note

I've used 2 commits in this PR. Originally, in the 1st commit, I've made the encoding a bit longer with token ID to look something like `st.on_tt.rt_gt.ac:1f65761e-1c69-40a2-82da-2d8aa5e39a8a` .
  - The `st` is shortcut for "session type" and `on` is shortcut for "online" session
  - The `tt` is shortcut for "token type" and `rt` is shortcut for regular token (not lightweight token)
  - The `gt` is shortcut for grant type and `ac` is shortcut for "authorization code" grant

But assuming that every "type" has always 2 characters long shortcut, I've rather updated it in the 2nd commit to have only 7 new characters instead of 18 characters. I planned to squash before merge (unless you think that we should rather use longer format for some reason, in which case the 2nd commit can be removed from the PR).

raw_findings.body: The generated token ID contains the reserved "na" shortcut instead of the newly defined "cc" shortcut, so decoding reports an unknown grant for a known client-credentials token.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A valid client-credentials token is issued with incorrect encoded context metadata.
raw_findings.impact: The generated token ID contains the reserved "na" shortcut instead of the newly defined "cc" shortcut, so decoding reports an unknown grant for a known client-credentials token.
raw_findings.root_cause: The generic token initializer now derives grant metadata exclusively from a ClientSessionContext attribute, but the client-credentials generation path was not updated to populate it.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Set Constants.GRANT_TYPE to context.getGrantType() on clientSessionCtx in ClientCredentialsGrantType before generateAccessToken, and add an integration assertion for the "cc" shortcut.
raw_findings.title: Client-credentials access tokens encode an unknown grant type
raw_findings.trigger: A client requests an access token with grant_type=client_credentials, whose direct generation path calls generateAccessToken without setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE on clientSessionCtx.

raw_findings.body: The RPT token ID uses "na" instead of PermissionGrantTypeFactory's "pg" shortcut, making the encoded grant context incorrect.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A known UMA grant is decoded from its access-token ID as unknown.
raw_findings.impact: The RPT token ID uses "na" instead of PermissionGrantTypeFactory's "pg" shortcut, making the encoded grant context incorrect.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new generic token-ID encoder requires per-call-site grant propagation, but the direct UMA token-generation path was omitted.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Populate Constants.GRANT_TYPE with OAuth2Constants.UMA_GRANT_TYPE before AuthorizationTokenService generates the RPT, and cover this flow with an integration test.
raw_findings.title: UMA permission tokens encode an unknown grant type
raw_findings.trigger: AuthorizationTokenService generates an RPT for the UMA permission grant using its directly constructed clientSessionCtx, which does not set Constants.GRANT_TYPE.

raw_findings.body: Legacy token-exchange access tokens contain "na" rather than the registered "te" shortcut, so consumers cannot recover their actual grant type.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Grant metadata differs by token-exchange provider even though both use the same registered grant type.
raw_findings.impact: Legacy token-exchange access tokens contain "na" rather than the registered "te" shortcut, so consumers cannot recover their actual grant type.
raw_findings.root_cause: Only the standard token-exchange path was updated to provide the attribute consumed by the new generic encoder.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Set Constants.GRANT_TYPE to OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE on the legacy exchange clientSessionCtx before generateAccessToken, and test both legacy and standard providers.

raw_findings.trigger: The legacy TOKEN_EXCHANGE provider executes AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient, which generates an access token without the Constants.GRANT_TYPE assignment added only to StandardTokenExchangeProvider.

validated_findings.body: The generated token ID contains the reserved "na" shortcut instead of the newly defined "cc" shortcut, so decoding reports an unknown grant for a known client-credentials token.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A valid client-credentials token is issued with incorrect encoded context metadata.
validated_findings.impact: The generated token ID contains the reserved "na" shortcut instead of the newly defined "cc" shortcut, so decoding reports an unknown grant for a known client-credentials token.
validated_findings.root_cause: The generic token initializer now derives grant metadata exclusively from a ClientSessionContext attribute, but the client-credentials generation path was not updated to populate it.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Set Constants.GRANT_TYPE to context.getGrantType() on clientSessionCtx in ClientCredentialsGrantType before generateAccessToken, and add an integration assertion for the "cc" shortcut.
validated_findings.title: Client-credentials access tokens encode an unknown grant type
validated_findings.trigger: A client requests an access token with grant_type=client_credentials, whose direct generation path calls generateAccessToken without setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE on clientSessionCtx.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch shows OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java line 109 sets clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType()) before token generation. ClientCredentialsGrantType extends OAuth2GrantTypeBase and uses tokenManager.responseBuilder().generateAccessToken() which calls createClientAccessToken->initToken. The context.getGrantType() is populated from formParams in the Context constructor (line 102). The claim that client-credentials path doesn't set the attribute is not supported by the evidence.

validated_findings.body: The RPT token ID uses "na" instead of PermissionGrantTypeFactory's "pg" shortcut, making the encoded grant context incorrect.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A known UMA grant is decoded from its access-token ID as unknown.
validated_findings.impact: The RPT token ID uses "na" instead of PermissionGrantTypeFactory's "pg" shortcut, making the encoded grant context incorrect.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new generic token-ID encoder requires per-call-site grant propagation, but the direct UMA token-generation path was omitted.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Populate Constants.GRANT_TYPE with OAuth2Constants.UMA_GRANT_TYPE before AuthorizationTokenService generates the RPT, and cover this flow with an integration test.
validated_findings.title: UMA permission tokens encode an unknown grant type
validated_findings.trigger: AuthorizationTokenService generates an RPT for the UMA permission grant using its directly constructed clientSessionCtx, which does not set Constants.GRANT_TYPE.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: AuthorizationTokenService generates RPT tokens but the claim about missing grant type propagation is speculative. The patch shows the encoder falls back to UNKNOWN for unrecognized grants, which is documented behavior. No evidence that UMA tokens specifically fail to decode - the UNKNOWN handling is intentional.

validated_findings.body: Legacy token-exchange access tokens contain "na" rather than the registered "te" shortcut, so consumers cannot recover their actual grant type.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Grant metadata differs by token-exchange provider even though both use the same registered grant type.
validated_findings.impact: Legacy token-exchange access tokens contain "na" rather than the registered "te" shortcut, so consumers cannot recover their actual grant type.
validated_findings.root_cause: Only the standard token-exchange path was updated to provide the attribute consumed by the new generic encoder.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Set Constants.GRANT_TYPE to OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE on the legacy exchange clientSessionCtx before generateAccessToken, and test both legacy and standard providers.
validated_findings.title: Legacy token exchange encodes an unknown grant type
validated_findings.trigger: The legacy TOKEN_EXCHANGE provider executes AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient, which generates an access token without the Constants.GRANT_TYPE assignment added only to StandardTokenExchangeProvider.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch shows StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java line 237 sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE. The claim about legacy token exchange is speculative - AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient is mentioned but no evidence shows it's actually missing the attribute setting or that it produces incorrect tokens.

validated_findings.body: Construction unexpectedly succeeds and encoding appends the literal string "null", potentially producing repeated or misleading token IDs instead of rejecting invalid input.
validated_findings.failure_mode: An invalid token context survives validation and is serialized with a non-generated raw ID.
validated_findings.impact: Construction unexpectedly succeeds and encoding appends the literal string "null", potentially producing repeated or misleading token IDs instead of rejecting invalid input.
validated_findings.root_cause: The constructor checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Change this check to Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").
validated_findings.title: Raw token IDs are not null-checked
validated_findings.trigger: A caller constructs AccessTokenContext with a non-null grantType but a null rawTokenId and passes it to the default encoder.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 73 shows Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") - the check validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId. This is a clear copy-paste bug where the wrong variable is checked, allowing null rawTokenId to pass validation.

validated_findings.body: getGrantType returns the originally cached value rather than the current form parameter, causing the token ID to encode the wrong grant shortcut.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Context accessors expose contradictory form and grant-type state.
validated_findings.impact: getGrantType returns the originally cached value rather than the current form parameter, causing the token ID to encode the wrong grant shortcut.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch caches a value derived from mutable state without keeping it synchronized with the existing mutator.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Derive getGrantType directly from the current formParams, or update grantType whenever formParams changes and prevent unsupported direct mutation.
validated_findings.title: Grant type becomes stale when form parameters are replaced
validated_findings.trigger: Grant code calls the existing setFormParams method, or mutates the supplied form map, after Context construction and then issues an access token.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch shows grantType is cached at construction time from formParams.getFirst(). While setFormParams exists, there's no evidence this method is actually called after construction in any real flow. The claim is speculative about a trigger that may not occur in practice.

validated_findings.body: The implementation emits a seven-character context prefix while the decoder requires exactly six characters, so tokens produced according to the documented contract cannot be decoded.
validated_findings.evidence: * @return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants. It can be useful for example in the tokens when the amount of characters should be limited and hence using full grant name
validated_findings.failure_mode: Extension authors receive incorrect implementation guidance.
validated_findings.impact: The implementation emits a seven-character context prefix while the decoder requires exactly six characters, so tokens produced according to the documented contract cannot be decoded.
validated_findings.root_cause: The public method documentation describes a shortcut length incompatible with the implementation and every built-in value.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Document that the default codec requires an exactly two-character, unique shortcut, including any reserved values or character restrictions.
validated_findings.title: The shortcut contract contradicts the fixed two-character codec
validated_findings.trigger: A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementer follows this new Javadoc and returns a three-character shortcut.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 30 Javadoc says '3-letters shortcut' but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider uses 2-character shortcuts (e.g., 'ac', 'cc', 'ro'). The documentation contradicts the implementation, which could mislead extension authors.

validated_findings.body: Encoding succeeds with a prefix of the wrong size, but getTokenContextFromTokenId later throws "Expected length of 6" for the resulting token ID.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The provider can generate token IDs that its own decoder rejects.
validated_findings.impact: Encoding succeeds with a prefix of the wrong size, but getTokenContextFromTokenId later throws "Expected length of 6" for the resulting token ID.
validated_findings.root_cause: The factory registers arbitrary shortcut strings while the default encoder and decoder assume a fixed two-character representation.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Validate during postInit and dynamic registration that every shortcut is non-null and exactly two characters, failing startup with a message identifying the offending factory.
validated_findings.title: Grant shortcut length is never validated before tokens are issued
validated_findings.trigger: A custom grant factory returns a shortcut whose length is not exactly two characters, including the three-character value suggested by the new interface Javadoc.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 74 shows grantShortcut is retrieved from gtf.getShortcut() and used without length validation. The decoder expects exactly 6-character prefix (2+2+2 for session+token+grant shortcuts). If a factory returns wrong-length shortcut, encoding succeeds but decoding fails.

validated_findings.body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit invokes the newly abstract method and can raise AbstractMethodError, preventing Keycloak startup until every extension is rebuilt and changed.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Previously loadable third-party grant providers become binary-incompatible during server initialization.
validated_findings.impact: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit invokes the newly abstract method and can raise AbstractMethodError, preventing Keycloak startup until every extension is rebuilt and changed.
validated_findings.root_cause: A new mandatory abstract method was added to an extension-facing provider interface without a backward-compatible default.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Provide a compatibility default for factories without shortcut support and encode them as unknown, or introduce a separate optional capability interface and document a migration period.
validated_findings.title: Adding an abstract factory method breaks existing custom grant providers
validated_findings.trigger: An installation upgrades with an OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation compiled against the previous interface.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 33 adds abstract method getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface. Existing third-party implementations compiled against prior interface will throw AbstractMethodError when postInit calls getShortcut(). This is a breaking API change without default implementation.

validated_findings.body: Recompilation fails, or an already compiled extension throws NoSuchMethodError when the constructor is invoked.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Existing extension code can no longer construct a derived Context in a source- or binary-compatible way.
validated_findings.impact: Recompilation fails, or an already compiled extension throws NoSuchMethodError when the constructor is invoked.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch deletes a public constructor from the grant provider context without a replacement.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the copy constructor and copy the newly added grantType field as well, or retain a deprecated compatibility overload.
validated_findings.title: Removing the Context copy constructor breaks existing grant extensions
validated_findings.trigger: A custom grant implementation is rebuilt or run after upgrade and uses the previously public Context copy constructor.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The LEFT source shows lines 102-116 contained a public Context(Context context) copy constructor that is removed in the patch. This breaks binary compatibility for extensions using this constructor.

validated_findings.body: The matcher normally returns true because it reads characters 3-4 instead of 4-5 and rejects equality rather than inequality, allowing grant-encoding regressions to pass integration tests.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Integration tests validate only the UUID suffix while effectively ignoring the expected grant metadata.
validated_findings.impact: The matcher normally returns true because it reads characters 3-4 instead of 4-5 and rejects equality rather than inequality, allowing grant-encoding regressions to pass integration tests.
validated_findings.root_cause: The matcher uses both the wrong substring indices and an inverted comparison for the grant field.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Require a six-character prefix and return false unless items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut).
validated_findings.title: Access-token event matcher does not verify the expected grant shortcut
validated_findings.trigger: A tested flow emits an access-token ID with an incorrect grant shortcut, such as "onrtzz:<uuid>" when "ac" is expected.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 483 shows 'if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false' - the logic is inverted. It returns false when the shortcut MATCHES, meaning the matcher passes when shortcuts DON'T match. This defeats the purpose of validating the grant shortcut.
